program.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk

requirements.text: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
requirements.source_phrase: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show identifiable chalk-like surface behavior, such as powdery smudging or soft chalk strokes, rather than only generic blur or grain?
nodes.criteria: pass: visible powdery, dusty smudging or soft strokes provide affirmative evidence of chalk-like treatment beyond generic blur or grain; fail: visible evidence affirmatively lacks chalk-like marks or surface behavior; unknown: the visible treatment cannot reliably be distinguished from generic filtering. Assess only this medium/treatment aspect; do not require drawing conversion or whole-image completion.
nodes.binding: Assess visible evidence of chalk-like medium or treatment only. Do not assess whether the image is a drawing or whether conversion covers the whole scene.

nodes.question: Does the image’s content read as a drawing rather than a photograph with blur, grain, or texture overlaid?
nodes.criteria: pass: evidence identifies drawn or illustrated rendering replacing photographic detail across the image’s content, including prominent subjects and surrounding areas; fail: evidence identifies retained photographic rendering with only blur, grain, or texture overlays; unknown: visible cues do not reliably distinguish drawing conversion from filtered photography. State the specific cues supporting the judgment and note any substantial photographic areas.
nodes.binding: Assess drawing-form conversion and its extent across the image. Do not assess chalk medium; do not treat sketch-like outlines, blur, or texture alone as proof of conversion.

nodes.question: Has the image been transformed into a drawing made from chalk?
nodes.criteria: Use only saved support observations. complete: n1 and n2 pass, and n2’s evidence explicitly establishes drawing conversion across the image’s content, with no substantial photographic areas remaining; n1 establishes chalk-like medium. partial: saved evidence affirmatively supports some requested progress, such as chalk-like treatment or drawing conversion, but complete conversion is not established; a fail or unknown does not by itself erase affirmative progress. absent: saved evidence affirmatively establishes that no requested transformation progressed; support failures alone are insufficient. unknown: evidence is insufficient to determine whether any requested transformation progressed. Do not infer visual facts beyond the supports; unrelated edits do not count.
nodes.binding: Target: the image. Reference: a drawing made from chalk. Combine the independent evidence for chalk medium and drawing form; do not inspect images or add requirements.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
